newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal's GDP grew 2.8 pct in 1996 - Finmin.
newsitem.headline: Portugal's GDP grew 2.8 pct in 1996 - Finmin.

text.p: Portugal's economy as measured by Gross Domestic Product (GDP) grew 2.8 percent in line with the government's earlier 2.5-3.0 percent forecast, Finance Minister Antonio Sousa Franco said.
He added that although inflation could quicken over the first months of 1997, the government was sticking to its forecast for average inflation over the year of 2.25-2.50 percent.
The 12-month rolling average rate, the government's yardstick, stood at 3.1 percent at the end of 1996.
Sousa Franco said that the pickup in inflation at the beginning of the year would be due to statistical factors, reflecting the exceptionally good performance in the first months of 1996.
Independent economists see the inflation rate slowing sharply from April or May.
Sousa Franco said that Portuguese economic growth last year was a percentage point higher than the European Union average.
He said that private consumption growth had exceeded the initial expectation for an increase of 2.2 percent.
Capital formation should also exceed the initial forecast for 3.0 percent growth, he said.
